newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine shares ride Wall St rally to strong finish.
newsitem.headline: Argentine shares ride Wall St rally to strong finish.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed higher Friday driven by a recovery in the Dow Jones .DJI.
The blue chip MerVal index ended 1.95 percent higher at 651.83 points.
"The local market is moving basically at the pace of traders who take the U.S. (Dow) industrials index and the long bond yield as their thermometer," said Andres MacEwan of Velox Inversiones.
"Besides that, institutional investors will let a week go by before plunging again into the market as they await the release of U.S. economic indicators."

"A decline in the last few days due to a rise in the long bond rate was deep, but considering the low volume traded (in Argentina) it looks like we have a correction," said Gonzalo Ballester, dealer for Galicia Valores.
The U.S. long bond rate held steady today at roughly 6.74 percent.
Argentine market volume was $15 million against $13.7 million on Thursday.
"The local market is very sensitive and volatile, with no genuine buy orders that in the last few months had protected it from international volatility," said MacEwan.
The broader general index .IGB rose 1.02 percent with 36 gainers, seven losers and 21 shares flat.
Main gainers among blue chips were Acindar, which rose 4.7 percent, and Molinos Ro de la Plata, up 4.3 percent.
"The market environment was calm. It was an atypical week due to the New Year holidays on Tuesday and Wednesday. Many dealers were not out there doing business," a broker said.
